NamedGraphScopeTest#explicitEmptyDataset.spec: SPARQL 1.1 Query §13.2 / §13.2.2 ("Each IRI is used to provide one named graph in the RDF Dataset"); how the graph for an IRI is obtained is implementation-defined
NamedGraphScopeTest#explicitEmptyDataset.note: RDF4J keeps FROM NAMED <http://example/empty> (no statements in the store) as an empty named graph, so GRAPH ?g {} gives one row; the engine drops a FROM / FROM NAMED IRI that is not in the local dataset (Factoidal issue 1032 records this as an allowed choice and asks only for a warning). Cross-check: data <urn:a> <urn:b> <urn:c>; SELECT ?g FROM NAMED <urn:x> { GRAPH ?g {} } gives no rows; ASK FROM NAMED <urn:x> { GRAPH <urn:x> {} } gives false. If the caller reads §13.2.2 as requiring the named graph, this becomes a defect.

BlankNodeReferenceConformanceTest#BNR-00.spec: SPARQL 1.1 Query §19.5 (IRI References: text matched by IRIREF must conform to RFC 3987 IRI-reference syntax) and §4.1.4 (Syntax for Blank Nodes)
BlankNodeReferenceConformanceTest#BNR-00.note: RDF4J BNR-1 (RDF4J-specific, vectors dated 2026-10-10) reads <_:id> as a reference to the stored blank node with that ID. In SPARQL <_:id> is an IRIREF; "_:id" is not an RFC 3987 IRI reference (no ALPHA scheme start; a relative first segment cannot contain ":"), so a conforming processor refuses the request, and blank nodes in a query (_:label, []) never denote a stored node. The engine reads <_:id> as the IRI "_:id" instead (see the iriref-rfc3987 defect), so it answers differently from RDF4J.
